name: Kormoran

sources.title: Finding Sydney Foundation — Final report of the search (2008), §3.3: the forward section upright, SSW/NNE with the bow to the north, about 90 × 20 m and up to 20 m high; debris field #1 nearly 1 km across around a piece of superstructure about 50 × 20 × 15 m; debris field #2 with pieces up to 35 × 15 × 15 m; positions of the three

Finding Sydney Foundation — search diary, 15-16 March 2008: the bow section from near the engine room to the stem, broken just aft of the bridge; raised flared forecastle, opening at hold 1; the mines of holds 4-6 blew the after part apart

WA Museum — wreck photographs: the starboard 15 cm gun under the forecastle, a 15 cm gun in No. 2 hold trained 135° to starboard, the port 2 cm gun raised with its flaps, the torpedo flaps, the starboard anchor in a piece of the ship's side in the debris field
German auxiliary cruiser Kormoran — ex Steiermark: length 164 m, beam 20.2 m

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q708046_kormoran.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. Node 'forward_section': the ship from the stem to just aft of the bridge (90 m), upright, with the flared forecastle and its two 15 cm guns (the starboard one with its flap down), hold 1 open, the 15 cm gun on its lift in hold 2 trained 135° to starboard, the front of the bridge superstructure torn aft, the raised 2 cm gun on the port side, the torpedo flaps. Node 'debris_field_1' (placed with 'pieces', 1.4 km NNE): a large piece of the after hull with the engine casing among hundreds of plates and frames, a jumble of wire, the starboard anchor in a piece of the ship's side. Node 'debris_field_2' (2.1 km N): the stern on its side and a few pieces. What the two after pieces really are is not known; their shapes, the spread of the debris (here a few hundred metres, really nearly 1 km) and the heading are approximate. A war grave. model_built.glb: the raider as she sailed in November 1941, disguised as a freighter. No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
